title: Understanding a work order and service boundaries
audience: Trainee or new worker on the solar panel cleaning track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Perform the named task within an approved scope and site safety rules
Explain and demonstrate safe decisions in realistic work situations
Provide observable evidence of work quality and appropriate escalation

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the solar panel cleaning track. Panels are usually mounted on roofs or elevated structures and are connected to DC and AC electrical circuits. Panels can produce voltage in daylight even when the rest of the system is off. Cleaning on this track does not include electrical work, isolation of the system, opening enclosures, or cable or connector repair. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Learning context and safe boundaries
instruction.body: A client requests an oven interior clean during a standard weekly service, but the work order lists only exterior wipe-down. The learner must follow the actual site induction, product instructions, employer procedures and supervisor direction. Do not undertake work beyond training or authorisation.

instruction.heading: Step-by-step field procedure
instruction.body:
1. Read the service type, included areas, exclusions, time allocation, special instructions and evidence requirements.
2. Distinguish routine cleaning from deep cleaning, repairs, high-risk work and handling valuables or personal documents.
3. Identify ambiguities before work starts; ask the designated supervisor for an approved change rather than improvising.
4. Document requests neutrally: what was requested, by whom, and what approval or alternative was offered.
5. Protect client privacy: avoid photographing personal information and share job records only through approved channels.

instruction.heading: Worked decision and reasoning
instruction.body: Client offers extra cash for an unapproved task. Decline the change politely and refer it for formal approval. The correct approach is to identify the applicable instruction, protect people and property, and document any departure from the original work order.

instruction.heading: Practice and feedback
instruction.body: Given three sample work orders, identify included tasks, exclusions, clarification questions and escalation decisions. The trainer observes each step, asks the learner to explain their decisions, and gives corrective feedback before reassessment.

instruction.heading: Quality and completion criteria
instruction.body: Evidence must show accurate scope interpretation, safe sequencing, correct tool/product selection, respectful communication, and reliable handover. Critical safety failures require stopping the practical and retraining.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Read the work order's service type, included areas, exclusions, time allocation, special instructions and evidence requirements before starting.
Separate routine cleaning from deep cleaning, repairs, high-risk work and any handling of valuables or personal documents.
Identify any ambiguity before work starts, and ask the designated supervisor for an approved change rather than improvising.
Decline any unapproved extra task politely, and refer it for formal approval.
Record each request neutrally: who asked, what was asked, and what approval or alternative was offered.
Avoid photographing personal information, and share job records only through approved channels.

Stop, make the area safe and tell your supervisor before resuming if conditions change, the task falls outside your authorisation, or work above ground level is requested without the required licence or authorisation.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: The service type, included areas, exclusions and evidence requirements are identified from the work order before work begins.
Ambiguous or out-of-scope requests are referred for formal approval rather than improvised.
Each request is recorded with who asked, what was asked and what approval or alternative was offered.
No personal information is photographed or shared outside approved channels.
summary: A work order sets the included areas, exclusions, time allocation and special instructions, and the cleaner reads all of them first.
Routine cleaning is kept separate from deep cleaning, repairs, high-risk work and valuables, so unclear requests go to the supervisor for approval.
Requests are recorded neutrally and client privacy is protected by sharing records only through approved channels.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be read on the work order before the first room is cleaned?
options: That the client has already paid for any extra tasks requested on the day
Only the time allocated, because the task list can be expanded on site
Whether an oven interior should be cleaned, since the client asked for it
The work order's included tasks, exclusions and special instructions, read before work starts

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do when a client asks for a change to the work order?
options: Refer the change to the supervisor for approval and record the request
Do the extra task now, because the client offered extra payment
Decline silently and tell nobody about the request
Use a stronger product on the oven interior to clean it quickly

knowledgeChecks.question: What record shows a work order's scope was honoured?
options: A verbal confirmation from the client at the doorstep and a note of the time the job ended
The completed work order checked against the stated scope, with declined or referred requests recorded
An oven interior cleaned without approval, as proof of extra effort and the cost of the extra product used
Photos of the client's documents, to show the work was done, and a copy of the bank statement
